models.name: Standard LSTM
models.architecture: Embedding (128d) -> LSTM (128 units, dropout 0.3) -> Dense (64) -> Output (3)
pros: Fast training time and low inference latency
Effective baseline for sequential review patterns
cons: Unidirectional context loses future sequence signals
Struggles with subtle sentiment shifts and complex negations

models.name: Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM)
models.architecture: Embedding (128d) -> BiLSTM (2x128 units, dropout 0.35) -> Attention Layer -> Dense (64) -> Output (3)
pros: Processes text in forward and backward directions simultaneously
Better captures contextual qualifiers (e.g. 'not good', 'hardly durable')
Significant gain over standard unidirectional LSTM
cons: Roughly 1.6x longer inference time than standard LSTM
Fixed word embedding limits deep polysemous word understanding

models.name: DistilBERT (Fine-Tuned)
models.architecture: DistilBERT Transformer (6 layers, 768 hidden, 12 attention heads) -> Classification Head (Dropout 0.2 -> Linear 768 -> 3)
pros: Full contextual self-attention across long review texts
Superior handling of nuanced clauses, sarcasm, and mixed reviews
Highest overall accuracy and balanced F1-score across all 3 classes
cons: Requires GPU for high-throughput batch training
